dedupe_keys.name: usda ers food access research atlas snap authorized retailer access map and large retailer access map

description: The Food Access Research Atlas (FARA) gives census-tract estimates of how many people live far from food retailers in the United States. It now has two parts: the SNAP-authorized Retailer Access Map (2025), built from all retailers authorised to accept Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits in June 2025, LandScan USA 2020 gridded population and the 2020–24 American Community Survey, with straight-line and road-network distances; and the Large Retailer Access Map (2019, with 2015 and 2010 editions), based on supermarket lists. Indicators flag low-income and low-access tracts at 0.5, 1, 10 and 20 miles and count children, elderly people, households without vehicles and SNAP households. The producer is the Economic Research Service of the U.S. Department of Agriculture. Coverage is the 50 states and the District of Columbia; territories are excluded. Files are Excel workbooks and zip packages downloadable without registration; no licence is stated on the pages read, and as a federal work it is free. Caveats: restaurants, farmers markets and delivery routes are excluded, access is measured only from home, unhoused people are not represented, and editions use different store lists, so they are not strictly comparable. Simulation uses: exposure of food access to store closures or network disruption, equity weighting in food supply resilience studies, and baselines for siting emergency food distribution. Related records: FEWS NET Data Explorer (data-fews-net-data-explorer) covers food security outside the US.
